explanation: Maintain the three largest values and the two smallest values at distinct scanned positions. Compare the product of the three largest with the product of the largest and two smallest.
correctness: A positive triple product uses either three positive values or two negative values and one positive value. The three largest maximize the first option; the two smallest together with the largest maximize the second. If no positive product exists, any zero gives the optimum zero. Without either possibility, all values are negative or the input has exactly three elements: the three largest maximize the all-negative product, and for exactly three elements both formulas use the only available triple. The tracked extrema preserve repeated values from distinct positions.
walkthrough: For [-8,-5,2,4], the first two negatives have product 40. Combining that pair with 2 gives 80, and later with 4 gives 160. Selecting the three numerically largest values would miss this result; tracking both low and high pair products preserves the winning candidate.
